en.name: Glass noodles, dried
en.summary: Dried glass noodles are almost pure mung bean starch, extruded and dried into brittle bundles. Sealed in a dry cupboard they keep about 2 years from purchase, and about 1 year once the bag is opened. Both figures are borrowed from dry pasta, because no food-safety authority publishes a home shelf life for 冬粉.
en.pantry: A sealed bag in a dry, ventilated cupboard keeps about 2 years from purchase; once opened, reseal it or decant it and use it within about 1 year. There is very little in a glass noodle for anything to live on except the starch, and with the water gone it is about as stable as a kitchen ingredient gets. The bundles are hygroscopic, though, so in a damp kitchen they go cloudy and soft and eventually mould from the inside of the bundle outwards. Keep them away from the sink and the rice cooker steam.
en.fridge: Dried glass noodles do not belong in the fridge — it is a humid place and they are a dry good. What does belong there is the same noodle once it has been soaked or cooked: at that point it is a wet starch food, in the same family as cooked rice, and it must be refrigerated promptly rather than left standing in its soaking water on the counter. Cool it quickly, keep it covered at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and do not let a bowl of soaked noodles sit warm for hours.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for dried glass noodles and they need none — a sealed bag in a dry cupboard already gives you a couple of years. Freezing the dry bundles adds nothing except condensation risk every time the bag comes out. Cooked glass noodles freeze poorly in any case: they are already soft, and thawing leaves them mushy and broken.
spoilage: Bundles gone cloudy, soft or bendy instead of glassy and brittle.
A musty or damp smell inside the bag.
Visible mould, usually starting deep in the middle of a bundle rather than on the outside.
Webbing, small moths or fine dust in a bag that has been open a long time.
tips: Reseal the bag properly or decant into a jar; humidity is the only real enemy.
Store away from the kettle, the rice cooker and the sink.
Soak only what you are going to cook; soaked noodles are a refrigerated food.
Buy small bundles rather than one large brick if you use them occasionally.

faq.q: How long do dried glass noodles keep?
faq.a: About 2 years from purchase sealed, and about 1 year once opened. Both numbers are borrowed from dry pasta.
Rarely, if kept dry. Damp is what ruins them — the bundles go cloudy and soft and can mould from the inside.

faq.q: How should soaked glass noodles be stored?
faq.a: In the fridge, covered, at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Once soaked or cooked they are a wet starch food and must not sit out.

zh.name: 冬粉
zh.summary: 乾燥冬粉幾乎是純的綠豆澱粉，擠壓成形後乾燥成一把把脆硬的麵束。密封放乾燥櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 2 年；開封後約 1 年。這兩個數字都借自乾燥義大利麵，因為沒有任何食安機關公布過冬粉的家庭保存期限。
zh.pantry: 未開封放乾燥通風的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 2 年；開封後密封或換罐，約 1 年內用完。冬粉除了澱粉之外幾乎沒有東西可供微生物利用，水分又已經被抽乾，算是廚房裡最穩定的食材之一。不過麵束很會吸水，在潮濕的廚房裡會變得混濁、發軟，最後從麵束內部往外發霉。請遠離水槽和電鍋的蒸氣。
zh.fridge: 乾燥冬粉不該放冰箱——冰箱是潮濕的地方，而它是乾貨。該進冰箱的是泡開或煮過之後的冬粉：那時候它已經是含水的澱粉食品，和熟飯同一類，必須盡快冷藏，而不是連泡麵水一起放在檯面上。請快速降溫、加蓋放 4 °C 以下，不要讓一碗泡開的冬粉溫溫地放好幾個小時。
zh.freezer: 乾燥冬粉沒有給冷凍期限，也不需要——密封放乾燥櫥櫃本來就有兩年左右。把乾麵束冷凍毫無好處，只會每次拿出來都多一次結露的風險。煮過的冬粉本來就不適合冷凍：它已經夠軟，解凍後只會爛掉、斷掉。
spoilage: 麵束變混濁、變軟、可以彎折，而不是透明脆硬。
看得見霉，通常從麵束中心開始，而不是外層。
開封很久的袋子裡出現絲網、小蛾或細粉屑。
tips: 袋口確實封好，或倒進密封罐；濕氣是唯一真正的敵人。
遠離熱水瓶、電鍋和水槽。
要煮多少泡多少；泡開的冬粉是冷藏食品。
偶爾才吃的話，買小把裝而不是一大塊。

faq.a: 未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後約 1 年。兩個數字都借自乾燥義大利麵。
保持乾燥的話很少壞。真正毀掉它的是受潮——麵束會變混濁發軟，甚至從內部發霉。

faq.q: 泡開的冬粉要怎麼保存？
faq.a: 加蓋放冰箱、4 °C 以下。泡開或煮過之後它就是含水澱粉食品，不能放在室溫。
